snippet.title: Putin kündigt massive Angriffe an — Deutschland streitet nur: Das steckt dahinter

Atomwaffen vor.

Und Europa? Europa streitet darüber,
ob man überhaupt mit ihm reden soll.

Putin eskaliert. Deutschland streitet.

snippet.title: GE Just Priced Itself Out of India's AMCA Fighter Jet: Indian Defence News
snippet.description:
AMCA Fighter Jet Engine Shock: GE's Triple Price Hike | Indian Air Force | Indian Defence Update |
Indian Air Force faces its biggest AMCA engine challenge! Is America's GE Aerospace putting India's AMCA stealth fighter at risk? Reports claim GE has sharply increased the price of the F414 engine, while negotiations with HAL have reportedly stalled. Now India is exploring Rolls-Royce and Safran as potential partners for the AMCA engine. Could this be another Tejas-style setback, or the moment India reshapes its defence future? Watch the full analysis on the AMCA, Indian Air Force, HAL, GE, Rolls-Royce, Safran, Tejas Mk2 and India's push for defence self-reliance. Watch this Inconnect News defence update for more details!

#India #IndianAirForce #Defence #Defencenews #IndianDefenceUpdate #AMCA #AMCAEngine  #HAL #DRDO #IndiaUS #IndiaUSDefence #Tejas #TejasMK1A #TejasMK2 #IndiavsPakistan #IndiaPakistanWar #IndiavsPakistan #PMModi #Geopolitics #news #currentaffairs #worldnews 

GE Just Priced Itself Out of India's AMCA Fighter Jet |
Is America's GE Aerospace delaying India's AMCA Fighter Jet? Reports claiming that negotiations between HAL and GE Aerospace over the AMCA Fighter Jet engine have stalled have sparked fresh debate over the future of India's most ambitious Indian Fighter Jet programme. Could this become another setback like Tejas Mk2, or will India now turn to Europe for a solution?

According to reports, GE Aerospace has significantly increased the price of the F414 engine during commercial negotiations with HAL, raising concerns over costs, technology transfer and production timelines. The engine was expected to power the first AMCA squadrons and Tejas Mk2, making it a critical part of the Indian Air Force modernisation programme. With DRDO and HAL leading the project, any delay could impact the IAF's future force structure.

Reports now suggest India has opened discussions with Rolls-Royce and Safran, both of which have reportedly offered extensive technology transfer and advanced engine development for future versions of the AMCA Fighter Jet. These developments come as delays in GE's delivery of F404 engines have already affected Tejas Mk1A production.
